title: Volume 1 Chapter 5: Skill Certification 1
content: But why? Who could it be? "Hajime, you mentioned that you were doing nails for a female friend in the garage."
"Ah, yeah..."
"Is that friend just one person?"
"Sayori... um, I did nails for her and another girl she brought along. No one else has come to the garage."
"Isn't there any rumor about it at school?"
"I haven't talked about the garage or the nails at school."
My father questioned me as if it were an interrogation. "So, no one else knows that you're doing nails in that garage?"
"Shouldn't be..."
For instance, Mio-chan. She might have heard about it from Sayori, but that doesn't mean she would call my father's workplace.
"Hmm. It's strange. I should have asked the person who called where they heard about it."
My father's expression remained stern. "Hajime, you understand that garage is primarily a place for me to work on cars, right?"
"Y-yeah. Of course."

"You know that the sign out front has the name of the construction company I work for and the phone number. Someone must have seen that sign and mistakenly thought we do nails at the construction company—at least that's what I think."
"I would think such a misunderstanding is unusual, but the voice on the phone sounded like a child. It could be someone around your age or even younger."
I see, that's why my father first asked about the number of friends and rumors at school. He assumed the call came from someone my age. (But who could it be...)
I began to recall recent events. The swimsuit photoshoot with Sayori and Karla—had nothing to do with the garage. I didn't mention the garage at that time either.

Sayori was reluctant to talk about having her nails done. Did Karla mention it to someone? I can't say for sure, but if she were to introduce my nails to someone, I feel like she would ask for my permission first. After talking a bit, I know she has that kind of sincerity. (And then...)
Sayori and Karla said they would post their matching nails on SNS. (But no, they said they would blur the background... Would anyone be able to identify it?)
They probably wouldn't even realize the background was the office of the garage. However, I couldn't think of any other possibilities.
If only I had checked the photos.
"Hajime."
As I was lost in thought, my father continued. "The president understands that I'm lending my son the unused part of the garage. The garage itself is my property. However..."
"Y-yeah."
"Now that inquiries about nails have started coming in, I can no longer say that you can use it freely."
I understood my father's reasoning.
Whether it was a misunderstanding or not, if it affected his company, he couldn't afford to lend it casually. Since he was doing me a favor by lending it, I couldn't say anything from my position.
"So far, nothing has caused trouble at work. But I can't say that nothing will happen in the future. Given the risk, I can't grant permission to continue with nails."
"But, Dad—"
"When you were just making plastic models, there were no such issues. So you can continue making models. But..."
My father showed no sign of listening to my side.
He was merely conveying a decision that had already been made. "I'm sorry for your friends, but you must stop inviting them to do nails."
I can no longer do nails in that garage.
What kind of expression would Sayori have upon hearing that?
"...I feel sorry to say this since you seemed to be having so much fun, but it can't be helped."
"Ugh."
When I first did Sayori's nails, I was the only one who could do it.
There was no other place but that garage.
Now, surely any other nail artist could do it. If a professional applied the techniques I discovered in the garage, they could easily do Sayori's nails.
But.
She said she liked my nails—
"Can I have a moment, Dad?"
"A moment?"
"I need to clean up the tools... and I want some time to explain to Sayori and the girls."
"That's fine. But make sure to explain as soon as possible."
It seemed I wouldn't have much time.
"Got it. I'll hurry. Also—can I investigate what happened? It's pretty strange that someone who knows about the garage would call your workplace."
"That's fine, but..."
My father's frown relaxed slightly. He seemed perplexed as well.
"Even if I find out the details, whether I can grant permission again is a separate issue."
"That's fine. I just want to understand."
"Then do what you can."
My father was strict but not unreasonable.
He probably thought it was enough if I could come to terms with it. It was his way of showing kindness.
"But in three days, you need to explain to your friends and start cleaning up."
"...Understood."
I need to explain the situation to Sayori and Karla as soon as possible.
What kind of expression would Sayori have when she finds out she can no longer use the garage?
I sent a message to Sayori, saying I had something important to discuss. My fingers felt heavier and clumsier than with any previous task as I operated my smartphone.
We had just parted ways. Neither Sayori nor I expected "See you tomorrow" to turn into this.
"Eh!? The garage can't be used anymore!?"
The next day.
I called Sayori and Karla to a coffee chain near the school to explain the situation.
Sayori's eyes widened in disbelief at the unexpected turn of events.
Now that I think about it—today we were supposed to do another nail session. We could have met in the garage.
Since my father said he couldn't lend the garage for nails, I thought it would be best to avoid calling them there, even for the explanation.
"I'm sorry. Since I'm borrowing it from my dad..."
"Y-yeah, that's understandable. But why did someone call your dad's company?"
Sayori showed me her smartphone.

It was a two-shot photo with Karla taken in the garage. The background was blurred, and with the sparkling effects, it was hard to tell where they were. Yet, the nails they showcased stood out in high resolution.
As expected, she seemed well-versed in photo editing to make models look good.
"With a photo like this, there's no way anyone would know about the garage. It doesn't even have a phone number on it."
"Right..."
"Ugh, I can't accept this... I really liked that garage."
Sayori's tail trembled. It seemed to be an expression of her dissatisfaction.
The garage, which was supposed to be my personal workspace, had somehow become an important place for Sayori as well.
Is there really nothing I can do?
"By the way, Karla! What have you been doing this whole time?"
Karla, sitting next to Sayori, had been fiddling with her smartphone. Using her four arms in a unique way, her fingers moved in a complex manner that was hard to follow with the eyes.
"Hmm. It's impossible to identify us just from our photos... so I'm searching SNS. Ego search, tag search... various things..."
Suddenly, Karla's fingers stopped moving.
"I found it!"
Karla showed me her smartphone.
It was a post from a certain SNS. It showed a photo taken from outside the garage, capturing Sayori and Karla just as they were coming out through the door.
Since the garage's exterior was photographed, the sign with the company name was clearly visible.
"Haah!? What is this? Were we photographed without permission!?"
"Yeah, looking at the tags... found Karla-chan... cute nails... together with Sayori-chan... it seems they do nails here too... Oh no, they completely caught us coming out of this garage."
"This is invasion of privacy!"
Sayori exploded with anger, ready to breathe fire.
"How could they do this without permission... this is ridiculous!"
"Calm down, Sayori."
Karla had mentioned she was a popular model.
Sayori was also recognized by Mio-chan. It wouldn't be surprising if there were some overly enthusiastic fans.
"Are we talking about stalkers? Isn't that dangerous..."
"Hmm, this account seems to be from a kid, probably a middle schooler. They don't seem to be following us around..."
Karla operated her smartphone to investigate further.

"There aren't any other photos of us. So, my guess is that a fan happened to pass by and saw us coming out of the garage. When they checked Sayori's SNS, they saw the photo of our matching nails... and got excited, posting it on SNS."
"Oh."
Could Sayori's post have contributed to this?
"Since it's a little kid without much internet literacy, they probably thought we did nails at that garage and were so happy that they posted it... or something."
"So, no malice...?"
"That's all just speculation. But if it were a real stalker, they wouldn't post their own stolen photos online. They'd keep them for themselves."
Karla spoke as if she knew real stalkers, which was frightening.
Being a professional model, Karla must have had opportunities to learn about such issues.

"Fashion for demi-humans is difficult, so demi-human models tend to be popular among their kind... I wonder if the person who took that photo is also a demi-human. I don't want to blame them too much..."
Sayori murmured with her brows furrowed.
She had her own struggles with fashion, and the trouble of not being able to do nails must relate to that.
"Well, the person who took this photo called your dad's company—could that be possible?"
"Or maybe this photo spread, and it was seen by a girl of the same age. Either way, we need to have the post removed."
Karla started operating her smartphone with her four arms again.
"I just contacted my agency's manager and a magazine editor. They don't seem to have bad intentions, so if the agency contacts the poster directly, the spread should settle down quickly."
"From what I can see, it doesn't seem to have spread too much."
"Since it's a kid's account. Thank goodness it wasn't a massive spread leading to a huge scandal."
Karla said it casually.
No, I think the one who would suffer the most from a spread would be Karla, the model from the agency.
"Having fans is nice, but..."
Sayori muttered softly.
"Things like this aren't good. It's causing trouble for Azuma-kun too."
"Well, it's not like I'm troubled or anything..."
A post without malice. Probably the work of a younger girl. When I think of it that way, I don't feel much anger...
"No. Calling your dad's company is absolutely not okay. It has nothing to do with the nails we were doing..."
"That's true."
Sayori looked down.

After taking a sip of her café au lait, Karla said, "Our agency will probably issue a warning, and they should be able to get it removed. But if we have to explain the situation... do you think your dad will continue to lend you the garage?"
"I don't think so."
I shook my head.
"Even if the post is removed, it doesn't eliminate the risk of it spreading."
"Once something is on the internet, it's hard to erase the information."
"My father understands that. As long as there's a possibility of inquiries coming to the company, I don't think it will be allowed."
"That's right."
Karla seemed to have a certain understanding. She looked disappointed but accepted the situation.
Meanwhile, Sayori looked like she was about to cry. Biting her lip in frustration and sadness.
"So, we can't go to the garage anymore."
"I'm sorry."
When I apologized, it felt like it confirmed that we really couldn't go anymore.
Even so, I had no choice but to say it. Even if I found out the circumstances thanks to Karla, I didn't have enough material to convince my father.
"No, it's fine. It's not your fault, Azuma-kun."
"I'm really sorry."
"Don't worry about it. It was originally my selfishness..."
It was a place I borrowed from my father.
If my father says no, I have no choice but to comply.
"But we can still do nails somewhere else—"
"No, if we do that, it might cause trouble for you again, so I can't ask for that. It would be better to wait a while and see how things go."
"That's..."
Sayori was right.
For now, it would be best to step away from nails. For both of us.
"No one is at fault! It can't be helped! So let's end this conversation! Ahh, I'm so thirsty after talking about such heavy stuff!"
Sayori changed the subject and took a sip of iced tea.
It was clear she was forcing a bright attitude. I didn't know what to say to her painful smile.
"Yeah. I'm thirsty too."
I could only say that, swallowing the bitter coffee.
In the end.
I gave up on doing nails in the garage.
As my father instructed, I decided to clean up the tools.
I wanted to do something about it, but—without being able to persuade my father, there was nothing I could do.
The post that had captured Sayori and Karla had been deleted shortly after. It was probably because Karla's agency contacted them.
I tried explaining the situation to my father, but ultimately, his stance didn't change. He judged that the risk was still present.
At school, in class, Sayori was just as usual.
She didn't show any signs of being down. Surrounded by friends, as always.
However, the nails she had on were the nail chips I had first made for her. It made sense since Sayori hadn't been able to apply polish.
It had been a week since I told Sayori and Karla that they couldn't do nails.
Previously, Sayori would come to the garage almost every day, especially during the week of the photoshoot.
Now, she hadn't come to the garage for an entire week.
What had happened to her nails? If I didn't grind them soon, they would become unpaintable again.
Would she be satisfied with just the chips?
No, that couldn't be. Since Sayori was so particular about her nails, she wouldn't be satisfied with just the first nail chips I made.
If I were to put it in Sayori's words, it would be something like "I'm not feeling it."
But there was nothing I could do.
I could no longer do nails in the garage. I was the one who told Sayori that.
Sayori accepted it and was now not coming to the garage.
(I wonder how the nails under the chips are doing...)

If it were before I knew Sayori, I could have just taken it at face value when I saw her laughing with her friends. I would have thought she was bright and had no worries, completely different from me.
But now it's different.
She has her own struggles. No matter how cheerful she seems in class, she must be troubled inside about not being able to paint her nails.
For some, not being able to do nails might not be a big deal. But I know it’s a huge concern for Sayori.
So, what can I do for her?
"Hey, Azuma, your face, your face."
Miyabe said to me, surprised. "Why do you look so scary?"
"Ah, just... lost in thought..."
"Oh, is it about a new plastic model? When you finish the next one, show it to me."
"Yeah, if I make one."
I felt bad for Miyabe, but I wasn't in the mood to assemble a new model right now.
Sayori glanced over here for a moment.
Frustrated that I couldn't do anything for Sayori, I instinctively averted my gaze from her.
Even though I couldn't call Sayori and the others to the garage anymore.
I still went to the garage after school. I wasn't prohibited from entering, and I had things to do.
"I need to clean up the nail tools."
My father had told me to clean up as soon as possible.
However, I felt so lazy about it that even after a week, the nail supplies remained untouched. I would get scolded by my father if I didn't organize them soon.
I could just put the easy-to-organize tools in a plastic case and take them home, but—
What should I do with the sofa and chairs I prepared, knowing Sayori would come? The nice tablecloth and the slightly stylish desk lamp?
It would be hard to keep them in my room, so I would have to store them in the back warehouse.
"...Sigh."
When I start thinking too much, my hands tend to stop.
I sighed and began to carry each of those nail salon-like items into the warehouse.
Gradually, the garage transformed back into the scene it was when I used it alone.
The same sight as when I was absorbed in making plastic models.

(…How long am I going to keep moping around?) It’s not like I’m going to be returning to anything before Sayori arrives. Sayori and I originally had no connection at all—so even if things went back to the way they were, it shouldn’t be painful. That’s what I thought, but still… I couldn’t help but feel that I wanted to do more nails for Sayori.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/3wiWZ22.jpeg
“Ah.”
While tidying up, I noticed that the magazines Sayori had brought to the garage were still there. She had left them all behind.
“Throwing them away would be a bit much, huh? I guess I’ll have to return them at school…?”

If I returned these magazines, Sayori would probably make a sad face again. It would be like declaring that she no longer needed any nail information. But then again, keeping them forever wouldn’t be right either…
Then I realized that there was a book in the magazine rack where I had tossed Sayori’s magazines. It was the textbook for the Nail Certification.
Qualifications—maybe it wouldn’t be a bad idea to try for them. But if I couldn’t do nails for Sayori anymore, it might not mean much. (Qualifications… studying…)
—Really?
Suddenly, an idea popped into my head. If I used the reason of getting certified, maybe I could continue using the garage? My head, which had felt heavy for so long, suddenly felt lighter.
Just like when I was absorbed in making plastic models, my mind became clear and filled with heat.

I interrupted my tidying and began reading the Nailist Certification textbook. Ideas for how to persuade my father started flowing into my mind. It didn’t take long for me to become confident that this would work. (This could work—right?)

I could still continue doing nails. Before I knew it, I had sent messages to Sayori and Karla, asking them to come to the garage tomorrow. There were still things I could do for her. Just that alone made me inexplicably happy.
“E-excuse me~…”
